perf.summary: Find does full path compression in two passes (find root, then rewrite), doubling pointer traversals; path-halving achieves near-identical amortized bounds in one pass.
perf.currentCost: First while-loop walks to root, second while-loop walks the same chain again rewriting parents: two traversals of the path per Find call.
perf.proposedChange: Replace with single-pass path halving: 'while (i != parent[i]) { parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]; i = parent[i]; } return i;'. One traversal, each node points to its grandparent.
perf.rationale: Path halving gives the same O(alpha(n)) amortized complexity as full compression but in a single pass with half the memory traffic and a shorter dependency chain per Find — a measurable win since Find is the hottest leaf across all connectivity operations.
perf.risk: Path halving does not fully flatten to the root immediately, so the exact parent[] contents differ from full compression — but Find/Connected/Union outputs (root identity, connectivity answers) are identical for all inputs. Only matters if a caller inspects intermediate parent[] structure, which it should not.

perf.summary: Init writes parent and size in one loop with two stores; size is a constant fill that could be memset-vectorized, and parent is an iota that Burst can vectorize.
perf.currentCost: n iterations doing parent[i]=i and size[i]=1 interleaved; the constant size fill is not expressed as a bulk memset.
perf.proposedChange: Keep parent[i]=i in its own tight loop (Burst can vectorize an iota with a base+index vector add), and fill size via a single bulk fill of 1s. Splitting the two stores avoids interleaving a varying store with a constant store and lets each loop vectorize cleanly.
perf.rationale: Separating the iota write from the constant write gives Burst two homogeneous, vectorizable loops instead of one mixed-store loop; the constant size fill becomes a streamable broadcast store.
